html:
The Molalla are a people of the western Cascade foothills of Oregon, from the Molalla River south toward the upper Umpqua and Rogue rivers.

They hunted deer and elk, gathered roots and berries and traded with the Klamath and the Cayuse to the east, while the Kalapuya held the valley below. Their language is now extinct. After the treaties of 1855 most were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation, alongside the Clackamas. The town of Molalla and the Molalla River keep their name.
